title: Intelligent Executor Routing
problem: Organization knows external executor families exist but lacks complete deterministic policy for self vs delegate, task classes, capability sufficiency, quota/cost, fallback, independent verification, and cold-start uncertainty.
impact: Without routing policy, persistent Bots may overuse expensive models, delegate trivial work, choose inconsistently, hard-code provider preference, exhaust quota, or use the builder as sole verifier.
desired_outcome: A persistent member can answer self vs delegate, required capabilities, eligible profiles, selection rationale, verification need, and evidence-insufficient behavior without inventing provider rankings. HOWL-005 defines policy and deterministic tooling only — no executor authentication or large benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Trivial and simple work default to SELF; external delegation requires expected value
Machine-readable task classes: trivial, simple, bounded, complex, critical (complexity does not override risk)
Claude, Codex, AGY remain registered; Astra added with honest needs-local-eval state
Selection policy forbids provider loyalty and permanent ranking; considers measured evidence, tools, risk, reliability, quota, cost/usage, latency, context, known failure modes
Prefer least-resource-intensive sufficiently capable executor; quality over cost when failure cost material
Critical/consequential work requires independent verification; builder not sole verifier
Security: task envelopes, child privilege <= parent, HowlFrame bypass forbidden, recursive delegation off by default, no secrets in routing config
Missing benchmarks produce visible uncertainty; never invent capability scores
Quota states: healthy, constrained, scarce, exhausted, unknown with conservative semantics
Cold-start and fallback/retry rules documented; multi-model fan-out not normalized
docs/EXECUTOR_ROUTING.md; orgctl route inspection if clean; schemas/validation/tests; context budgets pass
non_goals: Large external-model benchmarks or fabricated scores
Weakening HowlFrame, approvals, or privilege model
